title: VOLTAMMETRIC AND IMPEDANCE STUDIES OF ELECTRODEPOSITION OF Te AND ITS BINARY COMPOUNDS WITH Bi AND Sb USING CHOLINE CHLORIDE - UREA BASED ELECTROLYTE

segments.text: Cyclic voltammetry and AC impedance techniques were used to investigate electrode processes of Te, Bi, and Sb ions (introduced as TeO2, Bi2O3, SbCl3 precursors) on Pt electrode in a ionic liquid consisting in choline chloride - urea ( 1: 2 moles) eutectic as electrolyte.
The concentrations (mM) of precursors in the experiments were: 10.91 TeO2, 5.42 Bi2O3 + 5.45 TeO2, and 3.62 SbCl3 + 7.27 TeO2, respectively.
The working temperature was kept constant at 80 degrees C.
Cyclic voltammograms showed redox couples corresponding to cathodic deposition and anodic dissolution of Te, Bi-Te or Sb-Te.
Their cathodic peak currents increase with square root of scan rate, thus proving a diffusive controlled electrode process for all systems.

The processes of Te deposition, as well as BiTe and SbTe co-deposition, were also evidenced by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (Nyquist and Bode diagrams) performed in the same conditions of concentration and temperature.

title: Improvement of hotspot cooling in confinement space by corona discharge induced ionic wind

segments.text: Hotspot cooling is a significant problem in the thermal management of electronic devices.
With device dimension scaling down, the dissipation space becomes more and more confined making hotspot cooling challenged.
However, effective solutions are limited.
In this study, the feasibility of hotspot cooling by ionic wind in confined space is justified.
It is demonstrated that the hotspot in a confined channel can be suppressed effectively by ionic wind, which cannot be achieved by conventional pressure-driven flow even with a large Reynolds number.
The underlying physics is revealed by the secondary vortices.
The cooling strategies for a single hotspot and multiple hotspots are proposed.
There exists strong interplay between the secondary corona jet and the bulk flow.
Coupled mechanisms (impingement effect, barrier effect, and entrance effect) are explained to design a suitable electrode configuration for single hotspot cooling.
However, the design strategy for single hotspot cannot be directly used for multiple hotspots and a new design concept of intensify electrode pair is proposed.
It is also found that partial ground configuration is suitable for a single hotspot, while entire ground is better for multiple hotspots.
This work provides a potential means for hotspot cooling of electronic devices in confined space.

title: Convective couplings and thermal diffusion in ionic liquids

segments.text: We have performed thermal diffusion measurements of the molten mixture Agl/KI by a thermoelectric method in microgravity, these ones being disturbed on Earth by the free convection.
These experiments have left unanswered questions and we have planned new measurements in space using an optical method, in order to check the hydrodynamical regime of the liquid during the diffusion.
We have hence performed Earth experiments with a high viscosity mixture (LiCl, water) to assess the feasibility of these measurements.

title: Halogen-dependent optical response, band-edge alignment, and thermoelectric tunability in AlMgZ3 (Z = Cl, Br, I) cubic perovskites for photocatalytic water splitting and renewable energy applications: A first-principles investigation

segments.text: This study uses first-principles calculations to explore the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermodynamic, and thermoelectric properties of AlMgCl3, AlMgBr3, and AlMgI3 for potential energy-related applications.
The cubic perovskite structures are found to be structurally and thermodynamically stable based on tolerance factor analysis, formation energy calculations, and the Birch-Murnaghan equation of state.
The lattice parameters increase gradually from Cl to I due to the larger ionic size of the halogen atoms.
Mechanical property analysis shows that all compounds are mechanically stable, brittle, and anisotropic in nature.

Electronic band structure calculations reveal that AlMgCl3 and AlMgBr3 possess direct bandgaps of 3.15 and 2.80 eV, respectively, whereas AlMgI3 exhibits an indirect bandgap of 1.33 eV, indicating their suitability for photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications.
Optical investigations, including dielectric response and absorption spectra, demonstrate strong potential for solar energy conversion.
In addition, the calculated band-edge positions suggest that these materials may be useful for photocatalytic water splitting.
Thermoelectric transport properties obtained using the BoltzTraP code indicate dominant p-type conductivity and maximum ZT values of 0.780, 0.71, and 0.72 at 1200 K.
The quasi-harmonic Debye model further reveals the effects of temperature and pressure on thermodynamic parameters such as bulk modulus, heat capacity, thermal expansion coefficient, and volume.

Overall, the combination of these favorable properties highlights the potential of AlMgZ3 compounds for future optoelectronic and thermoelectric applications and motivates further experimental investigation.
